definitions.explanation: A deep, seemingly bottomless body of water or chasm. Used literally for deep waters and figuratively for profound, unknowable, or dangerous depths of the mind, evil, or abstract concepts.

examples.japanese: {深淵|しんえん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{覗|のぞ}き{込|こ}んだ。
⟦{人間|にんげん}→人間：03523_ningen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{心|こころ}→心：01321_kokoro⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{深淵|しんえん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{計|はか}り{知|し}れない。
examples.english: The depths of the human heart are unfathomable.

examples.japanese: {深淵|しんえん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覗|のぞ}く→覗く：02388_nozoku⟧⟦{者|もの}→者：12734_mono⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、{深淵|しんえん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{覗|のぞ}き{返|かえ}されて⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: He who gazes into the abyss finds the abyss gazing back into him.
examples.notes: A well-known paraphrase of Nietzsche, frequently quoted in Japanese.

notes:
REGISTER:
A literary and formal word. In everyday speech, ⟦{底|そこ}なし→底なし：20333_sokonashi⟧ or simply ⟦{深|ふか}い→深い：01211_fukai⟧⟦{穴|あな}→穴：01691_ana⟧ would be used. {深淵|しんえん} carries a philosophical or dramatic weight and appears frequently in literary, philosophical, and religious contexts.

USAGE:
The Nietzsche quotation {深淵|しんえん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覗|のぞ}く→覗く：02388_nozoku⟧⟦{者|もの}→者：12734_mono⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧… is widely known in Japanese and has made this word familiar even to non-literary readers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {深淵|しんえん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{覗|のぞ}く→覗く：02388_nozoku⟧: to gaze into the abyss
- {深淵|しんえん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{落|お}ちる→落ちる：01242_ochiru⟧: to fall into the abyss
- ⟦{心|こころ}→心：01321_kokoro⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{深淵|しんえん}: the depths of the heart
